persona.title: Pretend you are…
persona.text: Pretend you are Joy, 23, the only part-time helper at Hope Scholars Fund, a small charity in Ohio, USA, that pays school fees for students in Kenya. In America a charity must send yearly papers to the government on time, like the IRS Form 990 (the yearly report that keeps a charity tax free). The founder is worried a date will be missed, and today she asks you to put them all in one place.

lines: Welcome. This short video explains an app called Ahead of It, Nonprofit. You have never seen it before, and that is fine. In about four minutes you will know what it is for and how to use it.
A nonprofit is an organization that does good work and does not try to make a profit. For example a charity that pays school fees for students.
This app was made for small nonprofits in America. In America, a nonprofit does not pay tax, but only if it sends some papers to the government on time, every year.

The most important one is called Form 990. It is the yearly report a charity sends to the IRS, the American tax office, to stay tax free. If a charity misses it three years in a row, it loses its tax free status automatically.
There are other dates too: a state registration, board meetings with written minutes, insurance renewals, and thank you letters to donors.
Small charities often have only two or three people, all volunteers. Nobody is in the office. So a date is missed, and the charity gets into trouble.
Ahead of It keeps all these dates on one calm page, and reminds you thirty days before each one is due.
The app shows dollars, because it is American. If you like, you can think in shillings.
Now the screens. At the bottom there are four tabs: Next, Year, Library and Hand-off.

lines.t: Start with Library. It is a ready-made list of seventeen things small nonprofits must do, for example Form 990, the state registration, board meetings and the monthly bank reconciliation. Tap one, and it is added to your list.
Or tap the yellow Quick setup button. It shows the whole library with tick boxes. Tick what is yours, and tap Save.
Now tap Next. This is your main page. Overdue things are at the top, then Do something now, then Next 90 days, then Later this year.

lines: Tap the words of any item to open it. You can change the date in the box called Next due, and choose how often it repeats.
You choose how bad it is to miss it: No big deal, A hassle, or Costs real money. In the box Who else needs to know, you write a name, for example the board secretary. Then tap Save.

lines.t: Something not in the library? Tap the round orange button with the plus sign, type your own item and its date, and tap Save.

lines: Each item has buttons. When a reminder step is due, you see step tick. When the whole job is finished, tap done tick. The app moves the item to its next date by itself. For a monthly job, that is next month.

lines.t: The Year tab shows twelve months on one page, coloured by how bad each miss would be.
The Hand-off tab is for when you are away. It makes one page another person can work from. Here you also write whose list this is, for example the name of your charity.

lines: Everything stays on this phone. There is no account, and nothing is sent to anyone.
To start again with an empty list, scroll to the very bottom of the page and tap Start fresh. The app asks you twice before it erases anything.
In the test, you will help a small American charity that pays school fees for students in Kenya. Take your time, and if something is confusing, say so. That is exactly what we want to find.

challenge.intro: Now you are Joy at Hope Scholars Fund. The app is empty. Nobody will tell you which button to press — use what you learned. When you finish, tap Check my work.
challenge.start: Open Ahead of It · Nonprofit with the normal link (not the 🧪 test copy). If the welcome tour shows, tap 'skip the tour' → '✨ Start fresh with my own' → OK. If it does not show, scroll to the very bottom of the page and tap '🧹 Start fresh — erase this app’s data' → OK → OK. The page reloads. If a dark screen says 'Everyone has a list of things…', tap 'I'll explore on my own' at the bottom. You now see an empty list ('empty' at the top). If a small 'Got it ✓' box appears when you open a tab, just tap it. (Verified 10 Oct: all five checks false after this.)

tasks.text: Put the Form 990 on your list. Your charity's year ends in June, so this year it is due on 15 November 2026 — make that its date.
tasks.hint: It is in the Library under IRS. After adding it, open it on the Next page and change 'Next due', then Save.

tasks.text: Put the board meetings (with their written minutes) on your list. Kevin is the board secretary — make sure Kevin is told about it.
tasks.check: (function(){try{var d=JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem('goodstanding_v1')||'null');if(!d||!d.items)return false;var f=function(s){return d.items.filter(function(i){return String(i.id).indexOf('djex')!==0&&String(i.n||'').toLowerCase().indexOf(s)>=0})[0]};var i=f('board meeting');return !!i&&String(i.who||'').toLowerCase().indexOf('kevin')>=0;}catch(e){return false}})()
tasks.hint: Add it from the Library (Board). Open it and look for the box 'Who else needs to know'.

tasks.text: The money for Term 1 school fees must reach Kenya by 5 January 2027. It is not in the library. Add it yourself as 'School fees transfer'. If it is late, it costs real money.
tasks.check: (function(){try{var d=JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem('goodstanding_v1')||'null');if(!d||!d.items)return false;var f=function(s){return d.items.filter(function(i){return String(i.id).indexOf('djex')!==0&&String(i.n||'').toLowerCase().indexOf(s)>=0})[0]};var i=f('school fees');return !!i&&i.due==='2027-01-05'&&i.sev==='h';}catch(e){return false}})()
tasks.hint: Use the round orange ＋ button. Fill in the name and the date, and choose how bad it is to miss.

tasks.text: Today you finished this month's bank reconciliation (checking the bank statement against your records). Put it on your list and tell the app this month's job is done.
tasks.check: (function(){try{var d=JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem('goodstanding_v1')||'null');if(!d||!d.items)return false;var f=function(s){return d.items.filter(function(i){return String(i.id).indexOf('djex')!==0&&String(i.n||'').toLowerCase().indexOf(s)>=0})[0]};var i=f('bank reconciliation');return !!i&&Array.isArray(i.hist)&&i.hist.length>=1;}catch(e){return false}})()
tasks.hint: Add it from the Library (Money habits), then find it on the Next page. Saving it is not enough — one of its buttons says the job is finished.

tasks.text: If you are away, someone else will use this list. Write on it that it belongs to Hope Scholars Fund.
tasks.hint: Look in the Hand-off tab, in the box 'Whose list is this?'. Tap outside the box after typing.

ownWords.question: In your own words, what is this app for?
keyIdeas: keeps a small charity's important filing dates in one place
reminds you before papers like the Form 990 are due, so the charity stays legal and tax free
another person can take over using the hand-off list
